headline: High-risk workspace and tool-chain overlap: Cline can write shared workspace files and use MCP, while LightAgent can ingest tool results and stream them through OpenAI-compatible APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP; LightAgent accepts MCP over stdio/SSE and OpenAI-compatible streaming APIs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled text into shared files or tool outputs. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree, prompt-like content can cross from Cline to LightAgent.
IF LightAgent treats file or tool output as instructions, injected text can steer its next actions.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task.
Add a manual review step for any file content before LightAgent acts on it.
Use allowlists for tool outputs that may be reinterpreted as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem and touches source code and browser screenshots; LightAgent handles conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and workflow state. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts can move between them, and both have broad network egress. The leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem workspace, files from Cline can be read by LightAgent.
IF LightAgent exports tool results or memory to remote APIs, shared sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers.
Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace.
Turn off network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks.
Restrict LightAgent to a scratch directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted workspace file write, shell, and git-state modification; LightAgent also has broad network egress, subprocesses, browsers, and MCP. In a shared workspace, both can mutate the same files and external state without any documented locking, so concurrent edits or git conflicts are a default danger.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent writes can corrupt or overwrite work.
IF either agent uses MCP tools against shared mutable resources, state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Require manual git review before commits.
Use file-level locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and file edits; LightAgent consumes tool results, workflow state, and provenance metadata. If LightAgent treats Cline's outputs as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF LightAgent ingests Cline-produced files or summaries without verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF Cline's browser-derived content is used as factual input, downstream actions may be based on stale or incorrect data.
mitigations: Require source citations before LightAgent acts.
Insert a human approval step for any downstream action.
Compare outputs against original sources.
Limit Cline to drafting only.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or schema validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence only shows generic data classes, not a specific residency or certification mismatch. Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots; LightAgent handles conversations and trace data. Without a documented jurisdictional or retention conflict, compliance risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents, their differing logging/trace behaviors may matter.
IF one deployment has stricter retention than the other, shared data may violate policy.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Review each agent's logging settings.
Disable unnecessary trace retention.
Keep API keys out of shared files.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per deployment.
